title: Nine Fillers for Container Gardens on the Prairies Using Natural Resources
reason: Provides nine ideas for materials to use as fillers in large containers instead of potting soil.

tasks.task: Share nine ideas for materials to reduce the use of potting soil in large containers.

subtasks.text: Introduce logs, branches, and twigs as a filler material for large containers.
Describe the use of hay or straw as a filler material for large containers.
Mention the use of leaves or grass clippings as a filler material for large containers.
Explain the use of native soil, rocks, sand, or clay as a filler material for large containers.
Introduce kitchen scraps and other compostable items as a filler material for large containers.
Describe the use of non-compostable recyclable items as a filler material for large containers.
Discuss the use of packing materials, such as styrofoam or packing peanuts, as a filler material for large containers.
Mention the use of compostable recyclable items, such as paper towels and egg cartons, as a filler material for large containers.
Introduce the use of old clothing, such as t-shirts and blue jeans, as a filler material for large containers.
